text:
anya: Proposal — lightweight 'local-probe' + adaptive canary to speed private-model onboarding. Runs inside customer node, short golden-like checks, then conditional canary ramp. Sketch below.

matt: How is this different from smokehouse / mini-bench? Concerned about false negatives and non-determinism.

anya: local-probe = minimal determinism-focused checks (tokenization, logits-shape, kv-cache sanity) + semantic stability via embed-deltas. Only 100 samples, runtime matched to target quantized binary.

sylvia: exact_output_hashes won't work for chatty models. use cosine threshold on embeddings + token-distribution KL.

liam: Also must run the same kernel/quant config as target; else we get phantom mismatches.

anya: Agreed. Example config:
```yaml
local_probe:
  samples: 100
  max_tokens: 128
  checks:
    - kv_integrity: true
    - embed_stability_cosine: 0.92
    - kl_token_dist: 0.07
canary:
  initial_pct: 1
  ramp: [1,10,50]
  step_minutes: 15
  gates:
    - latency_p95_ms: 200
    - error_rate_pct: 0.1
```

bench-bot: quick run on `gpt-open-lite-v2` (simulated): local_probe pass=87/100, embed_cosine_avg=0.94, kl_avg=0.03, p95=180ms. note: this used quantized runtime path.

matt: 87% pass sounds borderline. What's our pass threshold? And what happens on marginal passes?

anya: default pass=90%. If between 80-90% -> tag 'needs-fullbench' and run full bench in background; but allow manual override for customer-paid expedited path.

sylvia: Operationally, how do we prevent canary from dispatching to production clusters? Need ephemeral isolation and QPS caps.

liam: propose: canary traffic goes to ephemeral canary-workers in dedicated pool with strict caps and automatic fallback. Also quota-metering to prevent cost shock.

anya: rollback policy: immediate rollback if p95>target or error_rate spikes > threshold. And write metric 'local_probe_signal' to model metadata for audits.

matt: We should add a 'shadow-compare' mode — mirror small percentage of prod traffic to the canary and compare outputs offline.

anya: yes — shadow-compare for 0.5-2% traffic by default for the first 24h of canary.

bench-bot: added PR preview: https://git.redwood/proposals/patch/12345 — includes runtime shim and canary config schema :eyes:

sylvia: I'll review runtime shim. matt/liam can you validate capacity control design?

matt: yep, i'll take capacity piece. quick question: do we discover problematic models earlier with this? sounds promising.

anya: goal is to catch obvious runtime/compat regressions fast and reduce full-bench load by ~40%. i'll draft RFC and add a playbook for 'pass / marginal / fail' actions.

liam: :thumbsup: ping me when RFC is up. we should schedule a 30m sync with infra + SRE.

anya: will do — thanks everyone.
